rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Its two-recital structure, description of a labor dispute affecting a substantial named industry engaged in interstate or foreign commerce, national-health-and-safety finding, and all three operative Board provisions closely match the child, with the industry, parties, strike status, and reporting date adapted. C04 is also an exceptionally close template, but C07 more closely matches the child's reference to a named industry and danger to both national health and safety. C24 shares a labor-dispute board structure but uses different Railway Labor Act machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between coal operators ... and certain of their employees ... involving wages or terms and conditions of employment
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between Swift and Company ... and certain of their employees ... involving wages
shared_material.explanation: The opening recital follows the same party–employee representative–subject-of-dispute formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: affecting a substantial part of the bituminous coal industry, an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several states and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce ... will imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.parent_excerpt: affecting a substantial part of the meat-packing industry, an industry engaged in trade or commerce among the several States or with foreign nations, or in the production of goods for commerce ... will imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, substantially shared statutory-finding language, adapted from meat packing to bituminous coal and from a threatened strike to an existing strike.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before April 5, 1948.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before April 1, 1948.
shared_material.explanation: The operative provision is nearly verbatim, changing only the deadline.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
